body.statement:
Fix \(\beta\in(0,1]\) and finite constants \(C_H,C_D>0\). Set \(q_j=1/T\), \(m=1\), and \(k=\lfloor T^{3/4}\rfloor\). For an array \(a=(a_{g,t}:1\le g\le t\le T-1)\), define
\[
A_t=\sum_{g=1}^t a_{g,t},\qquad v_{j,t}=a_{j,t}\mathbf 1\{j\le t\},\qquad d_j=(b^{\prime}a)_j=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\sum_{g=1}^t b_{(g,t),j}a_{g,t}.
\]
If
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}A_t=1,\qquad
\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}|A_t|\left(\frac{T-t}{T}\right)^\beta\le C_H\left(\frac{k}{T}\right)^\beta,\qquad
\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\inf_{c\in\mathbb R}\|v_t-cq\|_1\le C_D\frac{k}{T-k},
\]
then there is \(T_0=T_0(\beta,C_H,C_D)\) such that, for every \(T\ge T_0\),
\[
\sum_{j=1}^T\frac{d_j^2}{q_j}\ge\frac1{16}.
\]
Consequently, for no fixed \(C_E<\infty\) can arrays satisfying the three displays also satisfy \(\sum_jd_j^2/q_j\le C_ET/k^2\) for all sufficiently large \(T\). Thus the proposed certificate consisting of separate normalization, Holder-leverage, bounded-deviation-leverage, and \(O(T/k^2)\) shared-baseline-energy inequalities is impossible uniformly. This conclusion does not rule out every bounded lift and does not assert either equivalence or nonequivalence between \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)\) and the candidate diagnostic \(\rho_{N,T,m}\).
body.proof_tex:
Choose a fixed \(\lambda>0\) such that
\[
\eta:=C_H\lambda^{-\beta}<\frac18.
\]
For each \(t\), the continuous coercive function \(c\mapsto\|v_t-cq\|_1\) has a minimizer; fix one, call it \(c_t\), and write
\[
\varepsilon_t=v_t-c_tq,\qquad e_t=\|\varepsilon_t\|_1,\qquad D_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}e_t.
\]
The third displayed hypothesis gives
\[
D_T\le C_D\frac{k}{T-k}=o(1),
\]
because \(k=\lfloor T^{3/4}\rfloor\). Since \(\sum_jq_j=1\) and \(\sum_jv_{j,t}=A_t\),
\[
|A_t-c_t|=\left|\sum_{j=1}^T\varepsilon_{j,t}\right|\le e_t. \tag{1}
\]

Let
\[
J=\{t\in\{1,\ldots,T-1\}:T-t\le\lambda k\},
\qquad
E=\{j\in\{1,\ldots,T\}:j\le T-\lambda k\}.
\]
Integer inequalities are understood literally, so \(q(E)=|E|/T\ge1-\lambda k/T-1/T=1-o(1)\). If \(t\notin J\), then \(((T-t)/T)^\beta>(\lambda k/T)^\beta\). The Holder-leverage hypothesis therefore implies
\[
\sum_{t\notin J}|A_t|
\le \left(\frac{T}{\lambda k}\right)^\beta
\sum_{t\notin J}|A_t|\left(\frac{T-t}{T}\right)^\beta
\le C_H\lambda^{-\beta}=\eta. \tag{2}
\]
Using the normalization, (1), and (2),
\[
\sum_{t\in J}c_t
\ge \sum_{t\in J}A_t-\sum_{t\in J}e_t
=1-\sum_{t\notin J}A_t-\sum_{t\in J}e_t
\ge1-\eta-D_T. \tag{3}
\]

The baseline-loading definition and \(q_{>t}=\sum_{j>t}q_j\) give
\[
\sum_{j\in E}d_j
=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}H_t,
\qquad
H_t=-\sum_{j\in E}v_{j,t}
+A_t\frac{q(E\cap C_t)}{q_{>t}}. \tag{4}
\]
For \(t\in J\), every \(j\in E\) satisfies \(j\le t\), hence \(E\cap C_t=\varnothing\). Thus, by (3),
\[
\left|\sum_{t\in J}H_t\right|
=\left|-q(E)\sum_{t\in J}c_t-
\sum_{t\in J}\sum_{j\in E}\varepsilon_{j,t}\right|
\ge q(E)(1-\eta-D_T)-D_T. \tag{5}
\]
For \(t\notin J\), put \(p_t=q(E\cap C_t)/q_{>t}\in[0,1]\). Since \(A_t=c_t+\sum_j\varepsilon_{j,t}\), equation (4) becomes
\[
H_t=c_t\{p_t-q(E)\}
+p_t\sum_j\varepsilon_{j,t}-\sum_{j\in E}\varepsilon_{j,t}.
\]
Equation (1) yields \(|c_t|\le|A_t|+e_t\), and hence
\[
|H_t|\le |A_t|+3e_t.
\]
Together with (2), this implies
\[
\left|\sum_{t\notin J}H_t\right|\le\eta+3D_T. \tag{6}
\]
Combining (4)--(6),
\[
\left|\sum_{j\in E}d_j\right|
\ge q(E)(1-\eta-D_T)-\eta-4D_T.
\]
The right-hand side converges to \(1-2\eta>3/4\). Enlarging \(T_0\), if necessary, therefore makes it at least \(1/4\). Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz now gives
\[
\sum_{j=1}^T\frac{d_j^2}{q_j}
\ge\sum_{j\in E}\frac{d_j^2}{q_j}
\ge\frac{\left(\sum_{j\in E}d_j\right)^2}{\sum_{j\in E}q_j}
\ge\frac1{16},
\]
because \(\sum_{j\in E}q_j\le1\). Finally, \(T/k^2\to0\), so the lower bound \(1/16\) contradicts \(\sum_jd_j^2/q_j\le C_ET/k^2\) for any fixed \(C_E\) and all sufficiently large \(T\). This proves precisely the asserted certificate obstruction.
body.justification: The theorem isolates a design-specific obstruction created by reusing the same baseline cohort cells across all not-yet-treated contrasts.
body.gap: Published Gaussian modulus results condition on an operator and weights; they do not show that the natural staggered-DiD dual localization requirements force nonvanishing baseline Gram energy.
body.consumer: A future closed-form analysis must either use a certificate that avoids these separate leverage bounds or account explicitly for the nonvanishing shared-baseline term.
